summary: Saved the eight reviews consulted before interruption, including Dutch criticism. Seven are independently authored NDPR reviews, so journal concentration remains visible. Failed NDPR guessed URLs and inaccessible Kimmerle DOI are not counted.
next: Owner explicitly requests much greater exploration, worldwide and non-English evidence, well beyond 100 per broad target and toward 200 useful sources. Shift to diverse publishers and traditions.

sources.title: On What Matters, Volumes 1 and 2
sources.author: Mark Schroeder
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Schroeder praises the systematic achievement but argues that convergence can be overstated when Kantians reject the background assumptions. He distinguishes this project from Reasons and Persons.

targets.A: Critical evidence for books on moral progress and convergence.
targets.N: Scholarly reception of On What Matters, Volumes 1 and 2 as argumentative nonfiction.
targets.B: Explains and evaluates moral progress and convergence.
targets.P: Evidence for Derek Parfit's contribution and its reception.

sources.title: Epistemic Injustice: Power and the Ethics of Knowing
sources.author: Lorraine Code
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Code praises the connection between ethics, epistemology and power. Testimonial and hermeneutical harms affect people as knowers; collective prejudice complicates individual virtue remedies.

targets.A: Critical evidence for books on knowledge, credibility and social power.
targets.N: Scholarly reception of Epistemic Injustice: Power and the Ethics of Knowing as argumentative nonfiction.
targets.B: Explains and evaluates knowledge, credibility and social power.
targets.P: Evidence for Miranda Fricker's contribution and its reception.

sources.title: Death and the Afterlife
sources.author: John Cottingham
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Cottingham praises clear argument about humanity surviving one's death, but questions the exclusion of religious reflection. The review distinguishes collective survival from personal immortality.

targets.A: Critical evidence for books on future humanity and the significance of present projects.
targets.N: Scholarly reception of Death and the Afterlife as argumentative nonfiction.
targets.B: Explains and evaluates future humanity and the significance of present projects.
targets.P: Evidence for Samuel Scheffler's contribution and its reception.

sources.title: Creating Capabilities: The Human Development Approach
sources.author: Ingrid Robeyns
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Robeyns finds an effective general introduction. The capabilities approach evaluates substantive opportunities rather than resources alone, distinguishing Nussbaum's justice project from Sen's comparative assessments.

targets.N: Scholarly reception of Creating Capabilities: The Human Development Approach as argumentative nonfiction.
targets.B: Explains and evaluates human development and substantive opportunities.
targets.P: Evidence for Martha Nussbaum's contribution and its reception.

sources.title: Justice for Hedgehogs
sources.author: Gerald Doppelt
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Doppelt describes a systematic, readable defense of independent but mutually supporting moral values, interpreted through further value judgments rather than purely empirical tests.

sources.title: Democracy After Virtue: Toward Pragmatic Confucian Democracy
sources.author: Kenneth Winston
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Winston locates Kim between Confucian meritocrats and democrats. Kim challenges elite moral monopoly and treats pluralism as central to the problem of political legitimacy.

sources.title: Ethics in the Conflicts of Modernity
sources.author: Richard Kraut
sources.publisher: Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews / University of Notre Dame
sources.note: Kraut connects the book to After Virtue while noting renewed engagement with expressivism and Bernard Williams. MacIntyre's approach demands historical and social context for moral philosophy.

sources.title: Recensie: Sophie Bósèdé Olúwolé – Socrates en Òrúnmìlà
sources.author: Erik-Jan Hummel
sources.note: Hummel finds Oluwole accessible but sometimes repetitive and oversimplified. He disputes explaining Orunmila's obscurity mainly by mistranslation, emphasizing transmission and institutional reception.

targets.A: Adds Dutch criticism of a Nigerian comparative-philosophy book.
targets.N: Adds independent reception of oral-intellectual-history nonfiction.
targets.B: Preserves criticism of Oluwole's comparative method alongside its accessibility.
targets.P: Examines why Socrates and Orunmila receive unequal recognition.
